newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans spied on EU Balkan mission-TV network.
newsitem.headline: Germans spied on EU Balkan mission-TV network.

text.p: Germany's secret service (BND) infiltrated and spied on the European Union observation mission to the former Yugoslavia, the German television network ARD said on Wednesday.
The BND did not deny that charge. But it rejected claims made by ARD's "Monitor" magazine programme that it had supplied Moslem forces with ammunition.
In a release ahead of the programme's screening on Thursday, "Monitor" said the German secret service had delivered at least five ammunition shipments camouflaged as aid to Moslems.
The BND disputed the accusations made by the programme that it had violated the United Nations' weapons embargo.
"False claims will not become more true through repetition," the BND said in its statement.
"Monitor" made similar accusations in September, when the BND also denied them.
The programme said the secret service had recruited German EU observers for spying and paid them up to 15,000 marks for their work and said it could prove it with witness testimonies and documents.
